newsitem.title: USA: US Comptroller considers mix of bank and commerce.
newsitem.headline: US Comptroller considers mix of bank and commerce.

text.p: With the Clinton administration still deciding its stand on allowing combinations of financial and commercial companies, Comptroller of the Currency Eugene Ludwig told Congress on Thursday that resolving the issue will require great care.

While some in Congress and industry have explicitly rejected the concept, Ludwig left the door open to endorse the approach once the administration makes its decision as part of an overall package on bank reform.

"Permitting increased affiliations between commerce and banking is a complex issue requiring careful deliberations," Ludwig said in prepared testimony before the House Banking Committee's subcommittee on financial institutions.
"Changes in the law regarding such affiliations should be undertaken carefully, but we should keep in mind that there is no bright and unyielding line between banking and commerce," he said.
Ludwig noted that U.S. law separating banking and commerce has varied substantially over the past 200 years, sometimes with positive results.

"Companies created to promote the building of canals and railroads were sometimes endowed with bank powers to help finance them," Ludwig said. "It was not until the Bank Holding Company Act of 1956, that Congress prohibited commercial firms from combining with more than one bank."
Banking and commerce are still permitted within certain thrift holding company structures, he added.

Ludwig strongly endorsed allowing banks to expand into other financial service sectors. Last November, the comptroller's office said it would begin allowing banks, on a case-by-case basis, to enter non-banking businesses through subsidiaries.
"Consumers and businesses in many comunities would benefit if banks were allowed to engage in a wider range of activities," he said.
